body: Tested locally, it works as expected on all rendering methods. Code looks good to me.
Aside from some code style problems looks good, at least on the editor side. I'm not very familiar with 3D.

Works great now :slightly_smiling_face: 

One remaining issue is that the second light is never visible in the Compatibility method. It's strange because you *can* have multiple DirectionalLights at once in 3D, even with shadows enabled in Compatibility.
Tested again, a huge improvement to the material preview. Great work!

Tested locally, it works as expected on all renderers. Code and UX looks good to me. I think this is a great improvement already 🙂 | | | | -|-|-|-|- Custom environment/material work fine, even if you've set the floor material project setting to the same material that is being previewed. Runtime changes work even without having to switch materials in the inspector. Glow is now visible in material previews (since it's enabled in the default editor environment), which makes overbright parts of materials actually distinguishable in the preview. Some feedback: - Dragging the mouse with the middle mouse button held should pan the view, similar to the 3D editor viewport (or the left mouse button in the current preview). This allows the same UX pattern to work both ways. For future PRs: - The default checkerboard texture could have mipmaps generated, and the material could make use of anisotropic filtering to avoid Moiré patterns when the camera is near the floor (it's especially noticeable in motion). - Dragging the mouse with the right mouse button held (and Ctrl + Middle mouse button to match the 3D editor) could zoom in/out, so you could better appreciate small details. (This can't be done with the mouse wheel, as it's already used to scroll the inspector.) - While holding the right mouse button, moving the mouse upwards zooms in, moving the mouse downwards zooms out. - It's still difficult to distinguish enabled icons from disabled icons: Disabled icons should be made significantly darker to avoid this. This issue is pressent in the Mesh preview as well, so it's probably better to address it across all preview plugins in a single PR. - Since the **Editors > 3D > Preview Environment** project setting has a generic name (not tied to the material editor), it may be worth considering using it in the Mesh preview plugin as well as the Advanced Import Settings dialog's 3D view. - There could be more options for the preview mesh shape, I think the most important ones would be: - A rounded box material, so you can see how a material behaves with small bevels. The sharp box material should be kept separate. - A large horizontal plane (that overrides the floor checkerboard) with an infinitely repeating texture, so you can see how well a material tiles. - A dedicated tester mesh, similar to the testers found in the [Material Testers](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/3d/material_testers) demo. This is so you can see the impact of ambient occlusion in concave areas. Since this mesh is quite large, it would make zoom functionality even more important to have.
